The bill would strengthen the Federal-State system by increasing the number of workers covered, by requiring adequate benefit amounts...","explanation":"Both describe the same permanent reform proposal through closely corresponding components, especially expanded coverage and improved benefit levels."},{"child_excerpt":"The financial soundness of the system would be strengthened by increasing the amount of wages subject to taxation","parent_excerpt":"The bill would strengthen the Federal-State system... by improving financing","explanation":"The child elaborates the financing component previously presented in C02."},{"child_excerpt":"When enacted, the legislation will exert a stabilizing effect upon our economy, helping to maintain consumer purchasing power","parent_excerpt":"Enactment of the draft bill will... help stabilize the economy by increasing the purchasing power of such workers.","explanation":"This is a distinctive near-verbatim statement of the same economic mechanism."},{"child_excerpt":"workers who exhaust their regular benefits after March 31, 1962, will no longer be able to receive any unemployment compensation","parent_excerpt":"providing a Federal program of additional compensation... for workers who exhaust their regular benefits","explanation":"Both focus on additional protection for workers exhausting ordinary unemployment benefits, with the child urging action as the temporary protection approaches expiration."}]}
